# The long-title reveal arm compares two flush edges exactly, so a 7.6 µpx rect difference reds the dense Workstation control

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationNL.spec.mjs` — "a narrow long-title reveal stays contained and reads as an elevated pane" (the #18028 / PR #18038 containment arm, 420 × 900 viewport, the left rail's Dependency Graph Explorer reveal) — went red once in a whole-file run of the dense Workstation control on `dev@6bfb02fc16` (2026-09-23 11:32Z, headless Chromium on the seat's own Neural Link bridge, `NEO_NL_PORT` per #19066), right after #19111 merged. The same arm passed 4 of 4 in isolation two minutes later (`--repeat-each=4`, 10 s). The whole-file reading was 7 of 9: this arm and #19094's overflow frame (PR #19109 owns that one).

## The Problem

The arm compares two rendered edges that are equal by design with an exact `<=`:

```
expect(geometry.pin.right).toBeLessThanOrEqual(geometry.header.right);   // :2546
Expected: <= 226.12691497802734
Received:    226.12692260742188
```

The pin button sits flush with the reveal header's right edge; both numbers come from `getBoundingClientRect()` on different nodes, and they differ by 7.6 × 10⁻⁶ px. Nothing overflowed; the layout is the intended one, and the assertion reads float noise as a containment defect. Five assertions in the arm (`:2542`–`:2546`) compare rect edges exactly; the other four are between edges separated by padding today, so only this pair is at risk — until a stylesheet makes another pair flush.

Observation vs inference: the red and the four greens are observed; why the whole-file order produced the extra 7.6 µpx (the dense tour's tabs and split fractions left on the same page) is not classified and does not need to be — an exact comparison between equal-by-design edges is wrong at any order.

## The Architectural Reality

- The reveal header is a flex row and the pin is its last item, so the pin's right edge is the header's right edge by construction (the containment fix #18038 made the pin part of the header's box).
- Playwright rects are doubles from Chromium's layout units (1/64 px); sub-pixel disagreement between two nodes' rounded rects is a property of `getBoundingClientRect`, not a layout fact.
- The sibling containment arms in this file (`readDockChrome`, the split-chrome census) already read integers or use tolerances; this arm predates that convention.

## The Fix

Compare the pin's right edge to the header's with a tolerance below a pixel and above layout-unit noise — `expect(geometry.pin.right).toBeLessThanOrEqual(geometry.header.right + 0.5)` — and give the four sibling edge comparisons the same half-pixel allowance, with one comment naming why (rects are rounded per node). Test-only; no engine or app file changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 The five edge comparisons at `WorkstationNL.spec.mjs:2542`–`:2546` tolerate sub-pixel disagreement (≤ 0.5 px) and still fail on a real overflow — a control that widens the title by 1 px past the pin reds the arm.
- [ ] AC-2 The arm passes 5 of 5 in isolation and inside a whole-file run of `WorkstationNL.spec.mjs` on the seat's own bridge at the PR head.

## Out of Scope

- #19094 / PR #19109 (the whole-file run's other red); #19086's post-merge line (whole-file 9/9 ×3 on `dev`), which this arm's tolerance serves but does not close.
- The reveal's containment itself (#18028, closed): the layout is right; the measurement is what moves.
